question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate total milk production in the 24 major States of the United States in September 2026, in pounds (the report states it in million pounds), as it will be first reported in the USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service's monthly Milk Production report.

target.what: Total milk production in the 24 major States as defined by USDA NASS, in pounds (reported by NASS in million pounds), during September 2026, as it will be first reported in the USDA NASS monthly Milk Production report. This is a completed-month production flow, not annual or YTD production and not a
target.cadence: Monthly Milk Production report, typically released about the 20th of the following month
target.caveats: The exact NASS '24 major States' membership should be taken from the Milk Production report definition; if membership changed, use the definition in effect for the September 2026 first report. The target is the 24-state aggregate, not all-US production, and is the first-reported value before later r

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 24-state milk production should be anchored by the same series in prior Septembers and by 2026 year-to-date monthly values; recent year-over-year growth and the August-to-September seasonal pattern bracket the first-reported September value.
candidates.data_to_find: NASS Milk Production monthly 24-State milk production in million pounds for September 2021 through September 2025, plus January-August 2026 (or latest pre-cutoff months), ideally from report vintages using the same 24-state definition; include August 2026 and any pre-cutoff 2026 revisions. Minimum evidence: September 2023-September 2025 and 2026 monthly values through August.

assessment.note: All report the same NASS first-reported September 2025 24-state production total around 18.3 billion pounds, up 4.2% from September 2024. p34 gives the more precise first-reported figure; the others are rounded or duplicated releases.

Same August 2025 revised 24-state production figure, about 18.8 billion pounds. p2/p52 are rounded to 0.1 billion pounds, so they are less precise than the September 2025 and August 2026 three-decimal figures.
Same August 2026 preliminary 24-state production figure, about 19.17–19.2 billion pounds, up 1.8% year over year. p4 gives the precise first-reported 19.172 billion value.
All state the August 2026 24-state year-over-year production growth as 1.8%, from the same NASS August 2026 report.
Same September 2025 24-state milk cow inventory around 9.15 million head. p38 gives 9.146 million head; p3/p51 round to 9.15 million and note the 38,000-head increase over August.
Same September 2025 24-state milk per cow, 1,999 pounds, up 30 pounds from September 2024.
Same August 2026 24-state cow inventory, about 9.26 million head, up 15,000 from July and 151,000 from August 2025. p8 gives 9.264 million.
Same August 2026 24-state milk per cow, 2,070 pounds, up 4 pounds year over year.
Both state the August 2026 24-state milk-per-cow year-over-year gain as 4 pounds.
August 2026 state detail: sixteen states added a combined 393 million pounds and seven states lost a combined 48 million pounds, consistent with the 24-state total being up about 1.8% year over year.
State-level August 2026 growth/decline leaders: Texas, Kansas, and Wisconsin up sharply; California and Arizona down. This is consistent with the 24-state aggregate growth pattern.

State-level August 2026 year-over-year percentage changes are consistent with the reported state volume changes: Kansas and South Dakota strong, Texas/Wisconsin/Idaho/New York positive, Arizona/Utah negative.
Same U.S. total August 2026 milk production figure, about 19.9 billion pounds. This is a broader population than the 24-state target.
Same U.S. August 2026 year-over-year milk production growth, about 1.7%, slightly below the 24-state growth of 1.8%.
Same U.S. August 2026 cow inventory, about 9.71 million head, up 167,000 from August 2025.
Same U.S. August 2026 milk per cow, 2,049 pounds, down 1 pound year over year.
Same U.S. September 2025 total milk production, about 18.99 billion pounds, up 4.0% year over year.
Same U.S. September 2025 year-over-year milk production growth, 4.0%.
Same U.S. September 2025 cow inventory, 9.581 million head, up 228,000 from September 2024.
Same U.S. September 2025 milk per cow, 1,982 pounds, up 30 pounds year over year.
September 2025 state detail: twenty states added 789 million pounds and four states lost 54 million, consistent with the 4.2% 24-state growth.
September 2025 growth leaders: Idaho, Texas, and New York, consistent with the 24-state September 2025 growth pattern.
August 2026 dairy cow slaughter was 221,100 head, down from July but above August 2025. This is an administrative trace on herd change, not a direct production measure.
July 2026 culling data show slaughter slightly above year-ago levels and a culling rate near 2.3% of the herd. This is consistent with continued herd expansion but slower culling pressure.
Weekly and year-to-date culling through late August 2026 shows slaughter above 2025 but not at extreme levels. This supports a modestly expanding herd.
July 1, 2026 replacement heifers and dairy cow inventories point to herd stability/expansion rather than rapid contraction.

Both use a 2025 U.S. milk production total of 231.7 billion pounds; p200 is the October 2026 WASDE 2026 forecast of 236.9 billion pounds, implying annual growth. This is a forecast, not a September monthly observation.
Both reflect an earlier USDA/LMIC Q3 2026 U.S. milk production projection of about 0.9% year-over-year growth. The later August 2026 actual growth of 1.7–1.8% suggests this forecast is stale.

p42/p208 report U.S. September 2025 cows up 228,000 year over year; p156 reports the same 9.581 million level but up 238,000. The 10,000-head difference is likely a typo or revision, and p42/p208 are mutually consistent.

p13 and related U.S. yield points say August 2026 U.S. milk per cow was down 1 pound year over year. p63 lists a positive value of 1 with a name that could imply an increase, despite a quote saying down 1. The sign is ambiguous, so p63 is not used.
p4 and p5 together imply an August 2025 base, but p2 is rounded to 0.1 billion pounds. For growth-rate transfer, the reported 1.8% in p5 is more direct and less affected by rounding than p4/p2.

methods.rationale: Transfers the observed August 2026 24-state year-over-year growth of 1.8% to the first-reported September 2025 24-state level. This assumes August growth carries into September; it fails if September herd/yield growth diverges because of seasonal culling, weather, or HPAI. p150.role: month-over-month change in 24-state milk cow inventory, September 2025 vs August 2025, head

methods.rationale: Reconstructs September 2026 as August 2026 cow×yield (p8×p10) adjusted by the September-to-August ratios observed in 2025 for yield (p40/(p10-p11)) and cow inventory (p38/(p38-p150)). It assumes the 2026 September/August seasonal cow and yield ratios equal 2025; it fails if 2026 culling, heat stress, or yield seasonality differs materially.

This is a forecast-based route: it assumes annual U.S. growth is representative of 24-state September growth and fails if 2026 growth has slowed by September or if 24-state and U.S. growth diverge.

p5.role: 24-state milk production year-over-year change, August 2026 vs August 2025, percent

methods.rationale: Transfers the observed August 2026 24-state year-over-year growth of 1.8% to the first-reported September 2025 24-state level. This assumes August growth carries into September; it fails if September herd/yield growth diverges because of seasonal culling, weather, or HPAI. The reported percentage p5 is used directly instead of p4/p2 because p2 is rounded to 0.1 billion pounds.

p8.role: 24-state average milk cows in August 2026, head

p38.role: 24-state milk cow inventory in September 2025, head

p150.role: month-over-month change in 24-state milk cow inventory, September 2025 vs August 2025, head

methods.rationale: Reconstructs September 2026 as August 2026 cow×yield (p8×p10) adjusted by the September-to-August ratios observed in 2025 for yield (p40/(p10-p11)) and cow inventory (p38/(p38-p150)). It assumes the 2026 September/August seasonal cow and yield ratios equal 2025; it fails if 2026 culling, heat stress, or yield seasonality differs materially.

methods.label: m3

p34.role: 24-state milk production in September 2025, first-reported, pounds

p200.role: U.S. total milk production forecast for calendar 2026, pounds

p105.role: U.S. total milk production for calendar 2025, pounds

methods.rationale: Applies the October 2026 WASDE implied annual U.S. milk production growth (p200/p105) to the September 2025 24-state first-reported level. This is a forecast-based route: it assumes annual U.S. growth is representative of 24-state September growth and fails if 2026 growth has slowed by September or if 24-state and U.S. growth diverge.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
